questions.question: Name the four economic sectors and place each stage of the maize chain — growing, milling, retailing and cultivar research — into its correct sector.
questions.expected_answer: Primary extracts raw materials from nature; secondary transforms raw materials into products; tertiary provides services; quaternary handles knowledge and information. Growing maize is primary, milling it into mealie meal is secondary, selling and transporting it is tertiary, and breeding better cultivars in a research lab is quaternary.

questions.question: Distinguish GDP from GNP and state the approximate contribution of each sector to South Africa's GDP.
questions.expected_answer: GDP is the value of all final goods and services produced inside a country's borders regardless of ownership; GNP follows ownership — production by a country's citizens and companies anywhere in the world. Domestic follows the ground, national the passport. South Africa: agriculture about 2–3 per cent, mining under 10 per cent, secondary sector roughly a fifth, tertiary well over 60 per cent — a services-dominant structure.

questions.question: Explain why agriculture's share of employment is larger than its share of GDP, and state the general rule this illustrates.
questions.expected_answer: Raw farm produce sells cheaply so the sector's output value is low, but farming remains labour-intensive, needing many workers at modest wages — so its employment share (roughly double its GDP share) exceeds its money share. General rule: labour-intensive sectors carry a larger share of employment than of GDP, while capital-intensive, high-value-per-worker sectors like finance carry a larger share of GDP than of employment.
